- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during low sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — adjust upward, especially if recent history shows upward momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment is high and price surged.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is 5–10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged overreaction: if sentiment rises sharply but forecast lags, add 0.5–1.0% per day to forecast to catch momentum.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in trend — reduce first 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.
- High sentiment + recent price drop → forecast should not be overly optimistic — add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid overcorrection.
